question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Feud
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Harmony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Feud" (noun) means a long-lasting and bitter quarrel or hostility between two people, families or groups. (लंबे समय तक चलने वाला झगड़ा / वैमनस्य)

◦ Example: The two clans carried on a bloody feud for generations.

• Its antonym is "Harmony", which means agreement, peace and friendly relations. (सामंजस्य / मेल-मिलाप)

◦ Example: The neighbours lived together in perfect harmony.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Gross" means total (before deductions) or extremely unpleasant/vulgar — unrelated to feud.

• Option 2 "Peril" means serious danger or risk. (संकट)

• Option 4 "Vigour" means physical strength, energy and enthusiasm. (शक्ति / जोश)

NOTE

• Synonyms of feud: quarrel, vendetta, hostility, strife, discord, animosity.

• Antonyms of feud: harmony, accord, peace, concord, friendship, reconciliation.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

All these things happen/ because she do not / pay heed to my words.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. because she do not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is an error of subject–verb agreement. The subject "she" is a third person singular pronoun, so the auxiliary must be "does", not "do".

◦ Incorrect: because she do not pay heed to my words.

◦ Correct: because she does not pay heed to my words.

• In the simple present tense, a singular subject (he/she/it/a singular noun) takes "does/does not", while plural subjects (I/we/you/they) take "do/do not".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "All these things happen" is correct — "things" is plural, so the plural verb "happen" agrees with it.

• "pay heed to my words" is a correct expression; "pay heed to" means to give attention to / listen carefully to. (ध्यान देना)

NOTE

• Remember the rule of "s": in the simple present, either the subject carries the "s" (plural) or the verb carries the "s" (singular) — never both. She does, they do.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Professor said that I will be late for the lecture.
option_1: he shall be late for the lecture
option_2: he is late for the lecture
option_3: he would be late for the lecture
option_4: he may be late for the lecture
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. he would be late for the lecture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a sentence of indirect (reported) speech. Two changes are needed:

◦ The pronoun must change: the words are the Professor's, so "I" must become "he".

◦ The tense must be back-shifted: the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense, so "will" in the reported clause becomes "would".

◦ Correct: Professor said that he would be late for the lecture.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "he shall be late" — "shall" is not the back-shifted form of "will"; after a past reporting verb "shall" becomes "should".

• Option 2 "he is late" wrongly keeps the present tense.

• Option 4 "he may be late" changes the meaning by adding possibility, and "may" would become "might" after "said".

NOTE

• Back-shifting in reported speech: is/am → was, are → were, do/does → did, has/have → had, will → would, can → could, may → might, shall → should, must → had to.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Embarass.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Embarass" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Embarrass" — with double 'r' and double 's'. It means to make someone feel awkward, ashamed or self-conscious. (शर्मिंदा करना)

◦ Correct: Do not embarrass him in front of the whole class.

• Spelling key: EM + BAR + RASS (two r's, two s's).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Separate" (to divide; not joined) is correctly spelt — remember "there is a rat in sep-a-rat-e".

• "Accommodate" (to provide room/lodging for) is correctly spelt — double 'c' and double 'm'.

• "Definitely" (certainly, without doubt) is correctly spelt — it contains the word "finite", not "definately".

NOTE

• Word family: embarrass (verb), embarrassed / embarrassing (adjectives), embarrassment (noun). Commonly misspelt words in SSC exams: accommodation, occurrence, harass, millennium, questionnaire, maintenance.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Sell like hot cakes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Quick sell out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "sell like hot cakes" means to be sold very quickly and in large numbers; to be in great demand. (हाथों-हाथ बिक जाना)

◦ Example: The new mobile phone sold like hot cakes on the very first day of its launch.

• The nearest meaning among the options is "Quick sell out" — i.e., the entire stock is sold out quickly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Selling cakes" and 4 "Eating hot cake" are literal readings of the words; an idiom never carries its literal meaning.

• Option 3 "Being ignored" is the opposite of what the idiom means.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about demand and popularity: "go like hotcakes", "fly off the shelves", "in great demand", "a runaway success".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Andrew will playing basketball at the college tournament.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is playing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "will playing" is grammatically wrong — after the modal "will" we need the base form (will play), never the "-ing" form.

• The sentence describes a planned/arranged future action, which in English is normally expressed by the present continuous tense (be + V-ing). Since "Andrew" is singular, the correct auxiliary is "is".

◦ Correct: Andrew is playing basketball at the college tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "are play the" and 2 "are play" are doubly wrong — "are" does not agree with the singular subject "Andrew", and "are + play" is not a valid verb form.

• Option 4 "is played" is passive voice; Andrew is the doer of the action, so the active voice is required.

NOTE

• Present continuous = is/am/are + V-ing. It is used (i) for actions happening now and (ii) for fixed future arrangements — "She is leaving for Delhi tomorrow.".

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Hardik Pandya hit four ________ fours and scored 72 runs in the match.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. consecutive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consecutive" means following one after another in unbroken order; in succession. Four fours hit one after the other (ball after ball) are "four consecutive fours". (लगातार / क्रमवार)

◦ Correct: Hardik Pandya hit four consecutive fours and scored 72 runs in the match.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "continuous" means going on without any break in time (a continuous flow of water); separate boundaries are countable events, not an unbroken flow.

• Option 3 "ongoing" means still in progress (an ongoing project) — it cannot describe completed shots.

• Option 4 "constant" means unchanging or happening repeatedly and annoyingly (constant noise).

NOTE

• Useful distinction for SSC: consecutive = one after another in sequence (three consecutive wins); continuous = without interruption in time (continuous rainfall); continual = repeated with short breaks (continual interruptions).

question: Select the sentence that has NO spelling errors.
option_1: The doctor presribed some medicine to alleviate my parsistent cough, which has been boathering me for days.
option_2: The doctor precribed some medicine to aleviate my persistent cough, which has been bothering me for days.
option_3: The doctor prescribed some medicine to aleviate my parsistent cough, which has been boathering me for days.
option_4: The doctor prescribed some medicine to alleviate my persistent cough, which has been bothering me for days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The doctor prescribed some medicine to alleviate my persistent cough, which has been bothering me for days.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 4 spells every word correctly:

◦ "prescribed" — ordered/advised a medicine or treatment (PRE + SCRIBED). (नुस्ख़ा लिखना)

◦ "alleviate" — to make pain or a problem less severe (A + LLE + VI + ATE). (कम करना / राहत देना)

◦ "persistent" — continuing for a long time; not stopping (PER + SIST + ENT). (लगातार बना रहने वाला)

◦ "bothering" — troubling or annoying (BOTHER + ING). (परेशान करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "presribed" (→ prescribed), "parsistent" (→ persistent) and "boathering" (→ bothering).

• Option 2 misspells "precribed" (→ prescribed) and "aleviate" (→ alleviate).

• Option 3 misspells "aleviate", "parsistent" and "boathering".

NOTE

• Note the difference between "prescribe" (to recommend a medicine/rule) and "proscribe" (to forbid or ban). Also, "alleviate" (to relieve) vs "elevate" (to raise).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The athlete’s perseverance and mental toughness ________(facilitate) her to overcome adversity and achieve her goals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. enabled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Facilitate" means to make an action or process easier; to help bring something about. (सुगम बनाना / सहायता करना)

• Its closest synonym here is "enabled", meaning made it possible for someone to do something. (सक्षम बनाना)

◦ Correct: The athlete's perseverance and mental toughness enabled her to overcome adversity and achieve her goals.

• Grammatically too, "enable" takes the structure enable + object + to + verb ("enabled her to overcome"), which fits the sentence perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "restricted" (limited, kept within bounds) and Option 3 "limited" (restricted in amount/extent) are antonyms of facilitate.

• Option 4 "hindered" (obstructed, delayed) is also an antonym — and it contradicts the positive tone of "perseverance and mental toughness".

NOTE

• Synonyms of facilitate: enable, ease, assist, expedite, smooth the way for, promote.

• Antonyms of facilitate: hinder, impede, obstruct, hamper, thwart, restrict.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Throughout my career as a journalist, / I covered many important stories and / interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me / to share important information and insights with my readers.
option_1: to share important information and insights with my readers
option_2: I covered many important stories and
option_3: Throughout my career as a journalist,
option_4: interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The whole sentence is in the past tense ("covered", "interviewed"), so the relative clause verb must also be in the past tense: "which allowed me", not "which allow me".

◦ Incorrect: ... interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me to share ...

◦ Correct: ... interviewed numerous individuals, which allowed me to share ...

• This is an error of tense consistency (sequence of tenses) — all verbs describing the same past period must stay in the past tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Throughout my career as a journalist," is a correct introductory adverbial phrase.

• "I covered many important stories and" is correct (past tense).

• "to share important information and insights with my readers" is a correct infinitive phrase.

NOTE

• Structure: "allow + object + to + V1" (allowed me to share). Similar verbs: enable, permit, force, advise, request, encourage — all followed by object + to-infinitive.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Harish says / that his sister / loves to play / harmonium.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. harmonium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" is always used before the name of a musical instrument when we talk about playing it. So it must be "the harmonium".

◦ Incorrect: ... loves to play harmonium.

◦ Correct: ... loves to play the harmonium.

• Similarly: play the guitar, play the piano, play the flute, play the violin, play the sitar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Harish says" is correct — the singular subject "Harish" takes the verb "says".

• "that his sister" correctly introduces the noun clause.

• "loves to play" is correct — the singular subject "sister" takes "loves", and "love + to + V1" is a valid structure.

NOTE

• Contrast: with games and sports, no article is used — play cricket, play hockey, play football. With musical instruments, "the" is used — play the tabla.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Selling, purchasing, and using an illegally copied product is a criminal offence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a pirated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pirated" means illegally copied and distributed without the permission of the copyright owner — exactly the meaning of "an illegally copied product". (नकली / अवैध रूप से नकल किया गया)

◦ Correct: Selling, purchasing, and using a pirated product is a criminal offence.

• Note also that "pirated" begins with a consonant sound, so the article "a" is correctly used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "obsolete" means out of date / no longer in use — an old product is not necessarily an illegal copy.

• Option 3 "outlawed" means banned by law; a banned product is not the same as an illegally copied one, and the phrase does not convey "copied".

• Option 4 "crooked" means dishonest or bent — it describes people or conduct, not copies of products.

NOTE

• Related vocabulary: piracy (unauthorised copying), copyright, counterfeit (a fake imitation), plagiarism (copying someone's writing/ideas as one's own).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The hiring manager has already offered you the job; now, ________________ to accept or decline the offer.
option_2: the ball is in your court
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the ball is in your court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the ball is in your court" means it is now your turn to take action or make the decision. (अब फ़ैसला आपके हाथ में है)

◦ Correct: The hiring manager has already offered you the job; now, the ball is in your court to accept or decline the offer.

• The context fits perfectly — the manager has acted, so the decision now rests with the candidate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a penny for your thoughts" is used to ask someone what they are thinking about.

• Option 3 "pull your leg" means to tease or joke with someone. (मज़ाक करना)

• Option 4 "get your act together" means to organise oneself and start performing better.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from tennis — when the ball is in your half of the court, it is your turn to play. Similar expressions: "it's up to you", "your move", "the decision rests with you".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Oberon doesn’t like the way Demetrius ________ to Helena. (Credit: A Midsummer Night’s Dream)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. talks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause "Oberon doesn't like ..." is in the simple present tense, so the verb in the relative clause must also be in the simple present.

• The subject "Demetrius" is third person singular, so the verb takes "-s": "talks".

◦ Correct: Oberon doesn't like the way Demetrius talks to Helena.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "talked" (past tense) breaks the tense agreement with "doesn't like".

• Option 3 "talking" cannot stand alone as a finite verb — it needs an auxiliary (is talking).

• Option 4 "to talk" (infinitive) cannot serve as the verb of the clause "the way Demetrius ___ to Helena".

NOTE

• "A Midsummer Night's Dream" is a comedy by William Shakespeare; Oberon is the king of the fairies, and Demetrius and Helena are among the four young Athenian lovers in the play.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Let sleeping dogs lie
option_3: Leave an existing situation as it is
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Leave an existing situation as it is.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "let sleeping dogs lie" means to avoid raising an old issue that could cause trouble; to leave a situation undisturbed as it is. (पुराने झगड़े को न छेड़ना / जैसा है वैसा रहने देना)

◦ Example: Don't remind him of that old dispute — it is better to let sleeping dogs lie.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "To let somebody sleep" and 4 "To care for the pet" are literal interpretations of the words and are therefore wrong.

• Option 2 "To fall sick intentionally" has no connection with the idiom.

NOTE

• Idioms with a similar sense: "don't rock the boat", "leave well alone", "why look for trouble". Its opposite idea is "open a can of worms" (to create new problems by touching an issue).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A cage made for birds.

OR

A place for keeping the birds in a confined space.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Aviary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Aviary" is a large cage or enclosure in which birds are kept. (पक्षीशाला / चिड़ियाघर का पक्षी-बाड़ा)

◦ Example: The zoo's new aviary houses more than fifty species of birds.

• The word comes from the Latin "avis", meaning bird — the same root as "aviation" and "avian".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Aquarium" — a tank or building for keeping fish and aquatic animals.

• Option 2 "Apiary" — a place where bees/beehives are kept. (मधुमक्खी पालन स्थल)

• Option 4 "Arena" — a level area surrounded by seating, used for sports or performances.

NOTE

• Other useful one-word substitutes for animal enclosures: Kennel (dogs), Stable (horses), Sty (pigs), Byre (cows), Hive (bees), Vivarium (small animals/reptiles), Menagerie (a collection of wild animals).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Repulsive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Disgusting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Repulsive" means causing intense distaste or disgust; extremely unpleasant to look at or think about. (घिनौना / घृणित)

◦ Example: The rotting garbage gave off a repulsive smell.

• Its closest synonym is "Disgusting", which also means causing revulsion or strong dislike. (घिनौना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Attractive" (pleasing, appealing) is the antonym of repulsive.

• Option 2 "Reliable" means dependable/trustworthy — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Uniform" means unchanging or the same throughout — unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of repulsive: disgusting, revolting, repugnant, loathsome, abhorrent, sickening, offensive.

• Antonyms of repulsive: attractive, pleasant, appealing, charming, delightful.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The sergent brought in a lot of changes as soon as he was given charge.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. sergeant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "sergent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "sergeant" — a non-commissioned rank in the army, air force or police. (हवलदार / सार्जेंट)

◦ Correct: The sergeant brought in a lot of changes as soon as he was given charge.

• Spelling key: SER + GE + ANT — note the "ge" in the middle and the ending "-ant". It is pronounced /ˈsɑː(r)dʒənt/.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "seargeant" wrongly inserts an extra "a" after "se".

• Option 2 "sergeannt" wrongly doubles the "n".

• Option 3 "sergant" omits the "e" after "g".

NOTE

• Other rank/office words that are frequently misspelt in SSC exams: lieutenant, colonel, corporal, commissioner, superintendent, chauffeur.

question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The boy told his mother that he saw the most tall giraffe at the zoo.
option_1: The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.
option_2: The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.
option_3: The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.
option_4: The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tall" is a short (one-syllable) adjective, so its degrees are formed with "-er" and "-est", not with "more/most":

◦ Positive: tall

◦ Comparative: taller (used with "than")

◦ Superlative: the tallest (used with "the")

• "the most tall" is therefore wrong; the correct superlative is "the tallest".

◦ Correct: The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "the most taller" is a double comparative and is always wrong.

• Option 3 "the most tallest" is a double superlative and is always wrong.

• Option 4 "the more taller" is again a double comparative.

NOTE

• Rule: never combine "more/most" with "-er/-est". Long adjectives take more/most (more beautiful, the most beautiful); short adjectives take -er/-est (taller, the tallest).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Call the shots
option_1: To be a follower that makes less important decision
option_2: To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation
option_3: To be in a powerless position that follows orders
option_4: To be in a neutral position
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "call the shots" means to be in charge; to be the person who takes the important decisions and controls what happens. (निर्णय लेने वाला होना / कमान संभालना)

◦ Example: The new managing director now calls the shots in the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes a follower making unimportant decisions — the opposite of being in control.

• Option 3 "a powerless position that follows orders" is the antonym of the idiom.

• Option 4 "a neutral position" is unrelated to authority or decision-making.

NOTE

• Idioms with a similar meaning: "call the tune", "be in the driver's seat", "hold the reins", "run the show", "wear the trousers".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. watching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows "we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ______ the sun sink below the western isles". A present participle is needed to describe what the speakers were doing while sitting.

• "Watching" means looking at something for a period of time, and it fits the structure "watch + object + bare infinitive" — "watching the sun sink". (देखना)

◦ Correct: ... we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, watching the sun sink below the western isles.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "wallowing" means rolling about in mud/water or indulging in an emotion (wallowing in self-pity) — it cannot take "the sun sink" as its object.

• Option 3 "risking" means exposing to danger — meaningless here.

• Option 4 "practising" means doing something repeatedly to improve a skill — it does not fit.

NOTE

• Verbs of perception — see, watch, hear, feel, notice — are followed by object + bare infinitive (V1) for a completed action ("I saw him fall") and by object + V-ing for an action in progress ("I saw him falling").

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fancied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fancied" here means imagined; believed something to be so without certainty. (कल्पना करना / ऐसा प्रतीत होना)

• The narrator only *thought* he could see the wall of Lismore House — and the passage confirms this later with "But it was my fantasy, simply the image on my mind". So "I fancied I could glimpse ..." is exactly right.

◦ Correct: I fancied I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "groped" means to feel about with the hands in the dark — it does not take a clause like "I groped I could glimpse".

• Option 3 "imbibed" means to drink or to absorb ideas — grammatically and contextually wrong.

• Option 4 "translated" means to convert from one language to another — irrelevant.

NOTE

• "Fancy" as a verb has several senses: (i) to imagine ("I fancied I heard a voice"), (ii) to like or want ("Do you fancy a cup of tea?"), (iii) to be attracted to someone. The related noun is "fancy" = imagination.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a preposition of place showing that Lismore House stands upon its hilltop.

• "On" is used for a position on top of a surface — "the grey stone wall of Lismore House on its island hilltop". (पर / ऊपर)

◦ Correct: ... I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House on its island hilltop ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "off" indicates movement/separation away from a surface (he fell off the ladder) — the opposite of the sense required.

• Option 3 "aside" is an adverb meaning to one side; it cannot take the noun phrase "its island hilltop".

• Option 4 "for" expresses purpose or duration, not location.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: on (a surface — on the table, on the hill), in (an enclosed space — in the room), at (a point — at the door), above/over (higher than), under/below (lower than).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fantasy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contrasts what the narrator seemed to see with reality: "But it was my (4) ______, simply the image on my mind". The word must mean something imagined rather than real.

• "Fantasy" means a product of the imagination; a pleasant but unreal mental image. (कल्पना / मन की उपज)

◦ Correct: But it was my fantasy, simply the image on my mind ...

• It also links back neatly with "I fancied I could glimpse ..." in blank 2 — both come from the idea of imagining.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dribble" means a thin stream of liquid, or bouncing a ball in sport — meaningless here.

• Option 2 "straw" is dried stalks of grain or a tube for drinking.

• Option 4 "habitat" is the natural home of a plant or animal.

NOTE

• Word family: fantasy (noun), fantasise (verb), fantastic / fantastical (adjectives). Synonyms: illusion, daydream, imagination, reverie, figment.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. stared.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause is "like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) ______ too long at the sun". The preposition "at" signals a verb of looking, and "stare at" is the fixed collocation.

• "Stared" means looked fixedly at something for a long time. (टकटकी लगाकर देखना)

◦ Correct: ... like the image burned on to your eyes when you have stared too long at the sun ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "resumed" (to begin again after a pause) does not go with "at the sun".

• Option 2 "rusted" (to be corroded by rust) applies to metal, not to a person.

• Option 3 "blocked" (to obstruct) does not fit the structure "blocked too long at the sun".

NOTE

• Verbs of looking and their shades of meaning: glance (a quick look), glimpse (a brief, partial view), gaze (a long, steady look, often in wonder), stare (a long, fixed, sometimes rude look), peep/peer (to look with difficulty or secretly).

question: FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 matches were NOT held in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 was hosted by India from 11–30 October 2022. The matches were played at only three venues:

◦ Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar (Odisha)

◦ Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Fatorda, Margao (Goa)

◦ DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai (Maharashtra)

• No match was held in Gujarat. (गुजरात में कोई मैच नहीं हुआ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Spain won the title by defeating Colombia 1–0 in the final at Navi Mumbai; it was Spain's first U-17 women's world title.

• India participated as the host nation — its first appearance in a FIFA women's world event.

NOTE

• India had earlier hosted the FIFA U-17 (Men's) World Cup in 2017, which was won by England. FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.

question: Who among the following is one of the co-authors of the book, ‘Cracking The Code:My Journey in Bollywood’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ayushmann Khurrana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cracking The Code: My Journey in Bollywood" was co-authored by the actor Ayushmann Khurrana along with his wife Tahira Kashyap. (आयुष्मान खुराना)

• The book is part memoir and part guide, describing his journey from a small-town boy in Chandigarh to a leading Bollywood actor, and offering practical advice to aspiring actors.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ayushmann Khurrana first became known as the winner of the reality show MTV Roadies (2004) and made his film debut with Vicky Donor (2012), for which he won the National Film Award for Best Debut.

• He won the National Film Award for Best Actor for Andhadhun (2018) (shared with Vicky Kaushal for Uri).

• In 2020, he was named in TIME magazine's list of 100 most influential people.

NOTE

• Other books by film personalities: An Unsuitable Boy (Karan Johar), Khullam Khulla (Rishi Kapoor), Anything But Khamosh (on Shatrughan Sinha), The Substance and the Shadow (Dilip Kumar).

question: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique, describing a whole nerve cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Camillo Golgi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1873, the Italian physician and scientist Camillo Golgi developed the "black reaction" (*la reazione nera*), also called the Golgi stain — a silver-nitrate staining technique that made individual nerve cells visible in full detail for the first time. (कैमिलो गोल्जी — ब्लैक रिएक्शन)

• Using it, he published the first picture of nerve tissue showing a complete nerve cell (neuron) with its cell body and processes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Camillo Golgi also discovered the cell organelle now called the "Golgi apparatus/Golgi body" (1898) — the "post office of the cell", which modifies, packages and dispatches proteins.

• He shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (1906) with Santiago Ramón y Cajal for their work on the structure of the nervous system.

NOTE

• Option 1 Günter Blobel — Nobel Prize 1999, for protein targeting signals.

• Option 3 William Harvey — discovered the circulation of blood (1628).

• Option 4 Paul Ehrlich — Nobel Prize 1908; pioneer of chemotherapy and the drug Salvarsan.

question: In October 2022, Virat Kohli became the first Indian to complete how many runs in T20 cricket history?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2022, during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in Australia, Virat Kohli became the first Indian batter to complete 11,000 runs in T20 cricket (counting all forms of T20 — internationals, IPL and other domestic/franchise T20s). (विराट कोहली — 11,000 टी20 रन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kohli's famous unbeaten 82 off 53 balls against Pakistan at the MCG (23 October 2022) in that tournament is regarded as one of the greatest T20 innings; he was named Player of the Tournament in the 2022 T20 World Cup.

• He is also the highest run-scorer in the history of the T20 World Cup and of the IPL.

NOTE

• Virat Kohli's honours: Arjuna Award (2013), Padma Shri (2017), Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2018) and ICC Cricketer of the Decade (Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy, 2011–2020).

question: According to Sikh literature, the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev is celebrated on the full moon day of the Indian lunar month ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kartik.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the first Sikh Guru, is celebrated as "Guru Nanak Jayanti / Gurpurab / Prakash Parv" on the full moon day (Purnima) of the lunar month of Kartik (usually in November). (कार्तिक पूर्णिमा — गुरु नानक जयंती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Guru Nanak Dev (1469–1539) was born at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan) and founded Sikhism.

• His core teachings are summed up as "Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako" — meditate on God's name, earn an honest living, and share with others. He also started the tradition of langar (community kitchen).

• His hymns are compiled in the Guru Granth Sahib; the Japji Sahib is his best-known composition.

NOTE

• The ten Sikh Gurus run from Guru Nanak Dev to Guru Gobind Singh, who declared the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru in 1708. Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib.

question: Yakshagana is a folk dance that belongs to the state of __________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yakshagana" is a traditional folk theatre/dance-drama form of Karnataka, especially popular in the coastal districts (Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Uttara Kannada). (यक्षगान — कर्नाटक)

• It combines dance, music, spoken dialogue, elaborate costumes, towering headgear and vivid face make-up, and its stories are drawn mainly from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas. Performances traditionally run through the night.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The singer-narrator of a Yakshagana troupe is called the "Bhagavata", and the orchestra includes the chande (drum), maddale, harmonium and cymbals.

• Other folk/traditional forms of Karnataka: Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase, Kamsale, Huttari, Bayalata.

NOTE

• Folk theatre forms by state: Yakshagana (Karnataka), Kathakali/Koodiyattam (Kerala), Tamasha (Maharashtra), Bhavai (Gujarat), Nautanki (Uttar Pradesh), Jatra (West Bengal), Bhand Pather (Jammu & Kashmir), Swang (Haryana).

question: The brick temple of Bhitargaon is situated in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhitargaon Temple is located in the village of Bhitargaon, Kanpur district, Uttar Pradesh. (भीतरगांव मंदिर — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• Built in the early 5th century CE during the Gupta period, it is the oldest surviving brick (terracotta) temple in India and one of the earliest examples of a temple with a shikhara (spire).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is decorated with terracotta panels depicting Hindu deities and mythological scenes, and is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

• The Gupta age (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" and marks the beginning of the Nagara style of temple architecture.

NOTE

• Other famous Gupta-period temples: Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh (UP), Temple No. 17 at Sanchi (MP), and the Bhitargaon brick temple (UP).

question: Which of the following movements was founded in Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramakrishna Mission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ramakrishna Mission" was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897 at Belur, near Calcutta (Kolkata), Bengal, in the name of his guru Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. (रामकृष्ण मिशन — बंगाल)

• Its headquarters, the Belur Math, is on the banks of the Hooghly river in West Bengal. Its motto is "Atmano mokshartham jagad hitaya cha" — for one's own salvation and for the welfare of the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Arya Samaj — founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay (Mumbai); gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas" and started the Shuddhi movement.

• Satyashodhak Samaj — founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873 at Pune, Maharashtra, to fight caste oppression and promote education for the lower castes and women.

• Prarthana Samaj — founded in 1867 at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang, with M. G. Ranade as its leading figure.

NOTE

• Other reform bodies of Bengal: Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828), Atmiya Sabha (1815), Young Bengal movement (Henry Vivian Derozio).

question: On 15 August 1947, the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, raised the Indian National Flag above the _____________of Red Fort in Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lahori Gate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 15 August 1947, India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the Indian National Flag above the Lahori Gate of the Red Fort (Lal Qila), Delhi. (लाहौरी गेट — लाल किला)

• Since then it has become a tradition for the Prime Minister to unfurl the national flag at the Red Fort and address the nation on every Independence Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Red Fort was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1638 and 1648, when he shifted his capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad. Its architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.

• Its two main gates are the Lahori Gate (the main entrance, facing Lahore) and the Delhi Gate. Notable structures inside include the Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Rang Mahal, Moti Masjid and the Naubat Khana.

• The Red Fort was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

NOTE

• The famous couplet inscribed in the Diwan-i-Khas reads: "Agar firdaus bar roo-e-zameen ast, hameen ast-o, hameen ast-o, hameen ast" — "If there is a paradise on earth, it is this, it is this, it is this.".

question: ‘Mandarin’ is the official language of which neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mandarin" (Standard Chinese / *Putonghua*) is the official language of China, which shares a long land border with India. (मंदारिन — चीन की राजभाषा)

• Mandarin is the most widely spoken first language in the world by number of native speakers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Official languages of India's neighbours: Afghanistan — Pashto and Dari; Bhutan — Dzongkha; Sri Lanka — Sinhala and Tamil; Nepal — Nepali; Bangladesh — Bengali; Myanmar — Burmese; Pakistan — Urdu (and English).

• India shares land borders with seven countries: Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan; Sri Lanka and Maldives are maritime neighbours.

NOTE

• The India–China border is the Line of Actual Control (LAC), about 3,488 km long; the McMahon Line demarcates the boundary in the eastern sector. China's capital is Beijing and its currency the Renminbi (Yuan).

question: Which of the following is used to measure the total output of goods and services in an economy including depreciation during a specific period within country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gross Domestic Product (GDP)" is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country during a specific period (usually one year). (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद)

• The word "Gross" means depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) has not been deducted — so GDP includes depreciation; the word "Domestic" means it is measured within the country. Both conditions of the question are satisfied only by GDP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Key relationships:

◦ NDP = GDP − Depreciation

◦ GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)

◦ NNP = GNP − Depreciation

◦ NNP at factor cost = National Income

• "Net" always means after deducting depreciation; "National" always means including net income earned abroad.

NOTE

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The base year currently used for GDP series is 2011–12. The first estimate of national income in independent India was made by the National Income Committee (1949) headed by P. C. Mahalanobis.

question: Which of the following is NOT related to the sport of swimming?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Penalty Corner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Penalty Corner" (also called a "short corner") is a term from the game of hockey, not swimming. It is awarded to the attacking team for a defensive foul inside the striking circle. (पेनल्टी कॉर्नर — हॉकी)

• Breaststroke, Backstroke and Freestyle are all recognised swimming strokes/styles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The four competitive swimming strokes are Freestyle (front crawl), Backstroke, Breaststroke and Butterfly. In the individual medley, the order is butterfly → backstroke → breaststroke → freestyle.

• Other swimming terms: lane, lap, flip turn, false start, medley relay, dive.

• Other hockey terms: bully, dribble, push-in, long corner, green/yellow/red card, astroturf.

NOTE

• Swimming is governed by World Aquatics (formerly FINA); hockey by the International Hockey Federation (FIH). India's hockey legends include Major Dhyan Chand (whose birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day).

question: The East-West corridor, which is a part of the Golden Quadrilateral super highways, links which two cities of India from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Silchar and Porbander.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "East–West Corridor", part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) along with the Golden Quadrilateral, connects Silchar (Assam) in the east with Porbandar (Gujarat) in the west. (सिलचर – पोरबंदर)

• Its length is about 3,300 km, making it the longest of these corridors.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The "North–South Corridor" connects Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) with Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu), a length of about 4,000 km, with a spur from Salem to Kochi.

• The "Golden Quadrilateral" (about 5,846 km) links the four metros — Delhi – Kolkata – Chennai – Mumbai – Delhi. It was launched in 1998–2001 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

• These projects are implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), set up in 1988 (operational from 1995).

NOTE

• NH-44 (earlier NH-7) is the longest national highway in India (Srinagar to Kanyakumari, about 3,745 km); the shortest is NH-548 in Maharashtra.

question: What is the name of the seventh most abundant metal in the earth's crust, which is derived from the medieval Latin word 'Kalium'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Potassium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Potassium" has the chemical symbol "K", which comes from the medieval Latin word "Kalium" (itself from the Arabic *al-qalyah*, meaning plant ashes / potash). (पोटैशियम — प्रतीक K)

• It is one of the most abundant elements/metals in the earth's crust (roughly 2.1% by mass) and is an alkali metal of Group 1, with atomic number 19.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Potassium is a soft, silvery-white metal that is so reactive it must be stored under kerosene; it reacts vigorously with water producing hydrogen and a lilac flame.

• It was first isolated by Sir Humphry Davy in 1807 by the electrolysis of molten potash (KOH).

• Biologically it is essential for nerve impulse transmission, muscle contraction and maintaining fluid balance; bananas are a well-known dietary source.

NOTE

• Order of abundance in the earth's crust (by mass): Oxygen > Silicon > Aluminium > Iron > Calcium > Sodium > Potassium > Magnesium. Some other symbols from Latin: Na (Natrium – sodium), Fe (Ferrum – iron), Cu (Cuprum – copper), Ag (Argentum – silver), Au (Aurum – gold), Pb (Plumbum – lead).

question: What is the aim of Article 44 of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: To protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest
option_2: To separate judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State
option_3: To protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country
option_4: To secure for the citizen, a uniform civil code through the territory of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is To secure for the citizen, a uniform civil code through the territory of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP), states that "the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India". (अनुच्छेद 44 — समान नागरिक संहिता)

• A UCC would replace the different personal laws (on marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, etc.) of various communities with a single common set of laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other options correspond to different Articles:

◦ Article 49 — protection of monuments and places of artistic or historic interest.

◦ Article 50 — separation of the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

◦ Article 48A — protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976).

• DPSPs are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) and were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. They are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court).

NOTE

• Goa has long had a common civil code (a legacy of Portuguese rule), and Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to pass a UCC Bill (2024). The Supreme Court referred to Article 44 in the Shah Bano case (1985) and Sarla Mudgal case (1995).

question: Which of the following novels of Kamleshwar was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kitne Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Kitne Pakistan" ("How Many Pakistans") by Kamleshwar won the Sahitya Akademi Award for Hindi in 2003. (कितने पाकिस्तान — कमलेश्वर)

• The novel uses the device of an imaginary court ("adalat") in which history itself is put on trial, to explore Partition, communal violence and the repeated division of humanity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kamleshwar (1932–2007) was a leading Hindi writer, journalist and screenwriter, and a major figure of the "Nayi Kahani" movement along with Mohan Rakesh and Rajendra Yadav.

• He wrote screenplays/dialogues for films such as Aandhi, Mausam, Chhoti Si Baat and Rang Birangi, and was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2005.

• His other works include Kaali Aandhi, Ek Sadak Sattavan Galiyan and Jalti Hui Nadi.

NOTE

• The Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters, was established in 1954 and gives annual awards in 24 recognised languages; its highest honour is the Sahitya Akademi Fellowship.

question: Which of the following institutes was founded by MG Ranade and GV Joshi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poona Sarvajanik Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Poona Sarvajanik Sabha" was founded in 1870 by Mahadev Govind Ranade and Ganesh Vasudev Joshi (Sarvajanik Kaka), along with others, at Poona (Pune). (पूना सार्वजनिक सभा — 1870)

• It functioned as a bridge between the government and the people, submitting petitions on peasant grievances, famine relief and taxation, and is regarded as one of the forerunners of the Indian National Congress.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Abhinav Bharat — a secret revolutionary society founded by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (and Ganesh Savarkar) in 1904 at Nasik.

• The Indian National Congress — founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume, with W. C. Bonnerjee as its first president; its first session was held in Bombay.

• The Bombay Presidency Association — founded in 1885 by Pherozeshah Mehta, K. T. Telang and Badruddin Tyabji.

NOTE

• M. G. Ranade was also a founder of the Prarthana Samaj and the Indian National Social Conference (1887), and is called the "Father of Indian Economics" for his ideas on industrialisation.

question: Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia are eminent ______________ artists.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia are all eminent exponents of the Kathak classical dance form. (कथक)

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); the name comes from "Katha" (story) — the *kathakars* were storytellers who narrated epics through dance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kathak is marked by intricate footwork (tatkar), rapid pirouettes (chakkars), ghungroos and a blend of nritta (pure dance) and abhinaya (expression). It flourished in Mughal courts and absorbed Persian influences.

• Its three main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras (with Raigarh sometimes counted as the fourth).

• Other famous Kathak dancers: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Damayanti Joshi, Gopi Krishna, Uma Sharma.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Rani Machaiah is a __________ folk dancer who was awarded Padma Shri in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ummathat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rani Machaiah was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for her lifelong contribution to the "Ummathat" folk dance of the Kodava (Coorg) community of Karnataka. (उम्मथात नृत्य — कर्नाटक)

• "Ummathat" (also spelt Ummathat/Umathat) is a graceful women's folk dance of the Kodavas, performed in traditional Kodava attire in a circle, usually during the Kailpodh and Puthari festivals, with dancers holding cymbals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Lambadi" — a folk dance of the Banjara/Lambadi community, popular in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

• Option 3 "Gussadi" — a tribal dance of the Raj Gond tribe of Telangana; Gussadi exponent Kanaka Raju received the Padma Shri in 2021.

• Option 4 "Dhimsa" — a tribal dance of the Koraput region of Odisha and adjoining Andhra Pradesh.

NOTE

• The Padma Awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are announced every year on Republic Day eve and conferred by the President of India. In recent years many unsung grassroots artists ("People's Padma") have been honoured.

question: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
option_1: Debit cards are used for online transactions, while credit cards are used for in-person purchases.
option_2: Credit cards require a PIN, while debit cards require a signature.
option_3: Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.
option_4: Debit cards have higher interest rates than credit cards.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Debit card" is linked to the holder's savings/current bank account; when it is used, the money is deducted immediately from that account. You can spend only what you already have. (डेबिट कार्ड — अपने खाते से पैसा)

• A "Credit card" is a short-term borrowing instrument; the bank pays on your behalf up to a sanctioned "credit limit", and you repay later — with interest if you do not pay by the due date. (क्रेडिट कार्ड — उधार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong — both cards can be used online as well as at physical points of sale.

• Option 2 is wrong — in India both debit and credit card transactions at POS/ATMs normally use a PIN (two-factor authentication mandated by the RBI).

• Option 4 is wrong — a debit card charges no interest at all (it is your own money); it is the credit card that carries very high interest rates on unpaid balances.

NOTE

• Card networks: RuPay (India's own, by NPCI), Visa, Mastercard, American Express. NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) was set up in 2008 and also runs UPI, IMPS, BHIM, FASTag and AePS. Card issuance is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 has included Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 added the "Narikoravan" and "Kurivikkaran" communities to the list of Scheduled Tribes of Tamil Nadu. (नरिकोरवन और कुरिविक्करन — तमिलनाडु)

• These are traditionally nomadic, bird- and animal-hunting communities of Tamil Nadu; their inclusion gives them access to ST reservations in education, employment and legislatures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Under Article 342, the President, in consultation with the Governor, specifies the Scheduled Tribes of a state; any change in that list can be made only by an Act of Parliament.

• Similarly, Article 341 deals with the specification of Scheduled Castes.

• The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is a constitutional body under Article 338A (created by the 89th Amendment, 2003).

NOTE

• India's ST population is about 8.6% of the total (Census 2011). Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population, while Lakshadweep and Mizoram have the highest ST percentage. Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) number 75 across the country.

question: Which group of musicians were awarded by ‘Bharat Ratna’ from the following? (As of May 2023.)
option_2: Pandit Ravi Shankar and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>AR Rahman and Hariprasad Chaurasia
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the options, only Pandit Ravi Shankar (sitar maestro, Bharat Ratna 1999) and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana, Bharat Ratna 2008) have received the Bharat Ratna. (भारत रत्न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Musicians who have received the Bharat Ratna: M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Pandit Ravi Shankar (1999), Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001), Lata Mangeshkar (2001) and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (2008).

• A. R. Rahman (Padma Bhushan, two Oscars) and Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (Padma Vibhushan) have not received the Bharat Ratna; nor have Asha Bhosle, Kishore Kumar, Anu Malik or Udit Narayan.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954. It carries no monetary grant; the recipient receives a peepal-leaf-shaped medallion and a Sanad signed by the President. The first recipients were C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C. V. Raman (1954).

question: Which river is also known as Tsangpo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra river.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brahmaputra is known as the "Yarlung Tsangpo" in Tibet (China), where it rises from the Chemayungdung glacier near Mansarovar Lake in the Kailash range. (त्संगपो — ब्रह्मपुत्र)

• It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the "Siang/Dihang", becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam, and is called the "Jamuna" in Bangladesh, where it joins the Ganga (Padma) and finally the Meghna before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Its main left-bank tributaries are the Dibang, Lohit, Dhansiri and Kopili; right-bank tributaries include the Subansiri, Kameng, Manas and Sankosh.

• Majuli (Assam), the largest river island in the world, lies in the Brahmaputra.

• The Brahmaputra is one of the few male-named ("son of Brahma") rivers of India and is famous for its braided channels and heavy silt load, causing severe floods in Assam.

NOTE

• Total length of the Brahmaputra is about 2,900 km (roughly 916 km in India). The Bogibeel Bridge (2018) over it is India's longest rail-cum-road bridge.

question: What is the destination of the water drained off by the Nile river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mediterranean Sea.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nile, the longest river of Africa (about 6,650 km), flows northwards and finally drains into the Mediterranean Sea through a large delta in northern Egypt, near Alexandria and Damietta. (नील नदी — भूमध्य सागर में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Nile has two main branches: the White Nile, which rises from Lake Victoria (in the Great Lakes region), and the Blue Nile, which rises from Lake Tana in Ethiopia. They meet at Khartoum, the capital of Sudan.

• The Aswan High Dam in Egypt across the Nile created Lake Nasser, one of the largest artificial lakes in the world.

• Egypt is called the "Gift of the Nile" (Herodotus) because its civilisation grew along the river's fertile banks.

NOTE

• Longest rivers of the world: Nile (Africa), Amazon (South America — largest by volume), Yangtze (Asia), Mississippi–Missouri (North America). Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake and Lake Tanganyika the second deepest lake in the world.

question: Article 149 of the Constitution deals with _______________.
option_1: the qualifications required for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
option_2: the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
option_3: the term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
option_4: the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 149 of the Indian Constitution deals with the "Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG)". It provides that the CAG shall perform such duties and exercise such powers in relation to the accounts of the Union, the States and other authorities as may be prescribed by Parliament. (अनुच्छेद 149 — कैग के कर्तव्य और शक्तियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Related Articles:

◦ Article 148 — appointment, oath and conditions of service of the CAG.

◦ Article 150 — form of accounts of the Union and the States.

◦ Article 151 — audit reports of the CAG to be laid before Parliament/State Legislature.

• Parliament enacted the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under Article 149.

• The CAG is appointed by the President, holds office for 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, and can be removed only in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.

NOTE

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called the CAG "the most important officer under the Constitution of India". India's first CAG was V. Narahari Rao. The CAG heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and its reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
